response.answer: Innovative trends target A2A receptor signaling in CSF regulation through advanced mapping, pharmacologic validation, and preclinical testing to enhance CAR T-cell function and suppress tumor growth. Granulocyte macrophage-colony stimulating factor (GM-CSF) was originally identified as a growth factor for its ability to promote the proliferation and differentiation *in vitro* of bone marrow progenitor cells into granulocytes and macrophages. Many preclinical studies, using GM-CSF deletion or depletion approaches, have demonstrated that GM-CSF has a wide range of biological functions, including the mediation of inflammation and pain, indicating that it can be a potential target in many inflammatory and autoimmune conditions. ## Access through your organization. results.title: Genetic and pharmacological targeting of A2a receptor improves function of anti-mesothelin CAR T cells - PubMed
results.content: ## Save citation to file. ## Email citation. Go to My NCBI account settings to confirm your email and then refresh this page. doi: 10.1186/s13046-020-01546-6. # Genetic and pharmacological targeting of A2a receptor improves function of anti-mesothelin CAR T cells. * 1 Department of Medical Immunology, School of Medicine, Tehran University of Medical Sciences, Tehran, Iran. * 3 Department of Clinical Biochemistry, School of Medicine, Tehran University of Medical Sciences, Tehran, Iran. * 4 Department of Medical Immunology, School of Medicine, Tehran University of Medical Sciences, Tehran, Iran. * DOI: 10.1186/s13046-020-01546-6. # Genetic and pharmacological targeting of A2a receptor improves function of anti-mesothelin CAR T cells. doi: 10.1186/s13046-020-01546-6. * 1 Department of Medical Immunology, School of Medicine, Tehran University of Medical Sciences, Tehran, Iran. * 3 Department of Clinical Biochemistry, School of Medicine, Tehran University of Medical Sciences, Tehran, Iran. * 4 Department of Medical Immunology, School of Medicine, Tehran University of Medical Sciences, Tehran, Iran. * DOI: 10.1186/s13046-020-01546-6. Adenosine, a metabolite which is highly produced in TME, is known to mediate the suppression of anti-tumor T cell responses via binding and signaling through adenosine 2a receptor (A2aR). **Methods:** In this study, the expression of A2aR and the effects of its activation on the function of fully human anti-mesothelin CAR T cells (MSLN-CAR T), were analyzed. Afterwards, the molecular and pharmacological means to overcome the inhibitory effects of A2aR signaling on CAR T cell function were used. This was performed by targeting A2aR expression in MSLN-CAR T cells using various anti-A2aR shRNA sequences embedded in the CAR vector and an A2aR pharmacological antagonist, SCH-58261. Activation of adenosine signaling using adenosine analog led to the suppression of all major anti-tumor functions in MSLN-CAR T cells. Interestingly, CAR T cells that carried the anti-A2aR shRNA sequences were resistant to the inhibitory effects of adenosine signaling. **Conclusion:** Altogether, our results indicate that mitigating A2aR signaling by genetic targeting of the receptor might be a promising approach in improving CAR T cell function in an unreceptive microenvironment and could potentially improve the outcome of treatment in clinical settings. doi: 10.1007/s10555-007-9063-1.

results.title: Pharmacologic inhibition of CSF-1R suppresses intrinsic tumor cell growth in osteosarcoma with CSF-1R overexpression | Journal of Translational Medicine | Springer Nature Link
results.content:
Title: Pharmacologic inhibition of CSF-1R suppresses intrinsic tumor cell growth in osteosarcoma with CSF-1R overexpression | Journal of Translational Medicine | Springer Nature Link
Pharmacologic inhibition of CSF-1R suppresses intrinsic tumor cell growth in osteosarcoma with CSF-1R overexpression. We then investigated the anti-tumor effect and the mechanisms of action of pharmacologic inhibition of CSF-1R activity by pimicotinib (ABSK021), a highly potent and selective small molecule inhibitor of CSF-1R, in osteosarcoma models both in vitro and in vivo. ABSK021 effectively inhibited CSF-1R signaling and the proliferation of osteosarcoma cells with high expression of CSF-1R, by inducing cell cycle arrest and apoptosis. These findings conclusively demonstrated that pharmacological inhibition of CSF-1R activity by ABSK021 resulted in significant anti-tumor effects in preclinical osteosarcoma models with CSF-1R overexpression. We hypothesized that selective inhibition of CSF-1R could effectively suppress tumor cell growth in osteosarcoma with CSF-1R overexpression. In this study, we characterized CSF-1R expression and signaling in osteosarcoma cell lines and investigated the pharmacological effects of pimicotinib (ABSK021), a highly potent and selective small-molecule CSF-1R inhibitor discovered by Abbisko [20], both in vitro and in vivo models. Furthermore, colony formation assays revealed a significant reduction in colony-forming capability of murine K7M2 cells following treatment with ABSK021 (Fig. 2E and F), with minimal effects observed in the low-CSF-1R-expressing human 143B cells (Supplementary Fig. S1A and S1B). Inhibition of CSF-1R activity by ABSK021 effectively induces cell cycle arrest and apoptosis in high-CSF-1R-expressing osteosarcoma cells. The treatment effectively inhibits downstream signaling, suppresses tumor cell proliferation, and induces apoptosis, highlighting its therapeutic potential in CSF-1R-dependent osteosarcoma. In our study, we found that SJSA-1 and U2OS were low CSF-1R expressing cell lines and showed minimal effects on cell proliferation with treatment of ABSK021 (Fig. 2D) or PLX3397 (data not shown). Integrating data from in vitro cell lines and in vivo cell-, patient-derived xenograft models, we demonstrated that the anti-tumor effect is associated with high level of CSF-1R expression. Our study observed that the combination treatment results in enhanced inhibition of CSF-1R phosphorylation and the downstream ERK1/2 signaling pathway, a greater reduction in Ki67-positive proliferative tumor cells, and an increase in apoptotic cells compared to ABSK021 or chemotherapy alone. Pharmacological inhibition of CSF-1R with ABSK021 effectively suppressed tumor cell growth, reduced colony formation, and induced cell cycle arrest and apoptosis in CSF-1R overexpressed osteosarcoma cell in vitro.
